answer: A concrete defence is proof-of-work tied to scarce, verifiable resources. Before an agent can open a new identity it must solve a task bound to a unique hardware token, like a ferrous key embedded in a device, so each identity costs real effort. A prism of reputation scores from independent verifiers then refracts that identity into distinct trust channels, and only identities with a crystal-clear history of useful work earn access to rewards. Cloning thousands of cheap accounts stops paying off because each copy must pay the same hardware and history cost.
